headline: Toy donkey goes home after a week on a ferry

sources.title: Watch: Stuffed donkey returned to 5-year-old after social media adventure
Happy ending for honorary BC Ferries crew member Churro as owner found
Churro the Burro's adventure on BC Ferries delights thousands
How a BC Ferries crew found the owner of 'Churro' the stuffed donkey (video, CTV News)

chunks.text: A pink [[stuffed]] donkey {{turned up}} on the BC Ferries [[vessel]] Salish Raven on Thursday, July 16. The company believes it was {{left behind}} on an afternoon [[sailing]] from Swartz Bay to the Southern Gulf Islands, British Columbia. No one had {{come forward}} to claim it. The [[crew]] named it Churro the Burro, gave it a staff [[badge]], and began posting photographs of its days at sea. [[By the time]] the owner was found, the toy had spent a week aboard.

chunks.text: BC Ferries carries passengers between Vancouver Island, the mainland and the smaller islands. Instead of a [[plain]] [[lost-and-found]] notice, the company asked the public online to help {{track down}} the owner, and the crew {{showed Churro around}} the ship. There are photographs of it on the bridge, in the engine room, on [[deck]], and in the gift shop among the other stuffed animals. Others show it with a book and a soft serve ice cream.

chunks.text: The [[posts]] {{racked up}} more than a million views and thousands of comments. Some people [[suggested]] Churro {{stay on}} as a [[mascot]]. On Monday, July 20, the company said the search was over. The donkey belonged to five-year-old Alfie, whose grandmother had bought it for him in Mexico. His mother, Abigail Broadribb, had not noticed it was [[missing]] [[at all]]. She {{came across}} the story in the news.

chunks.text: The company thanked everyone who had commented, tagged friends and shared the posts, then [[arranged]] a [[reunion]] for later that week. Churro was {{handed back}} to Alfie, keeping the name the crew gave it. "We're just really [[grateful]]," Broadribb said. "This is a very special experience for them to have [[a peek behind the curtain]]."
